reasons: No tests or error-path checks are visible for this file.
Granting access has no confirmation step, even for the FULL level.
Errors on loading are reported only as a generic message without the server reason.
Loading uses any types, so wrong data shapes are not caught while coding.

terms.meaning: A web address that lets a doctor view selected records for a set time without making an account.
Another registered user who is allowed to help manage or view someone else's health records.
Cancel a previously given permission so it no longer works.
A short pop-up message that tells the user whether an action worked.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and page setup
sections.what: Brings in the icons, date helpers, buttons, drawer panel, notification helper and the connection to the server. It also marks the page as running in the browser.
sections.why: The page needs these tools to draw itself, talk to the server and show messages.
sections.watch_out: The page is marked as a browser-only component, so it cannot be rendered on the server.

sections.name: CaregiverPermissionsPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading permissions and revoking links
sections.what: Loads doctor share links and owned family profiles, selects the first profile if none is chosen, and revokes a doctor link when asked. A success or error message appears after each action.
sections.why: Keeps the list of links and profiles current after any change.
sections.watch_out: The load function depends on the selected profile, so its behaviour depends on which profile was chosen first.

sections.name: CaregiverPermissionsPage (part 2)
sections.title: Granting caregiver access
sections.what: Sends the chosen profile, caregiver email and access level to the server. On success it closes the form, clears the email and reloads. On failure it shows the server message or a default one.
sections.why: Creates a caregiver record on the server rather than trusting the browser to decide access.
sections.watch_out: The page does not check the email format before sending, so the server is the only place that rejects bad input.

sections.name: CaregiverPermissionsPage (part 3)
sections.title: Header and doctor link list
sections.what: Shows the page title, a back button to the family page, a Delegate Caregiver button, and a list of doctor links. Each card shows the doctor name, status (Revoked, Expired or Active), expiry date, view count and full link.
sections.why: Lets the owner see the state of each link at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The status shows Expired only when the server says so. If expiry times are wrong on the server, the status will be wrong too.

sections.name: CaregiverPermissionsPage (part 4)
sections.title: Revoke button and delegate form
sections.what: Shows a Revoke Link button on links that are still active. Also starts the Delegate Caregiver form with a profile picker and an email field that must belong to a registered user.
sections.why: Puts the action beside the item it affects and asks for the minimum needed to grant access.
sections.watch_out: The Revoke button has no confirmation step, so one click cancels a link straight away.

sections.name: CaregiverPermissionsPage (part 5)
sections.title: Access level choice and grant button
sections.what: Shows a drop-down with four access levels, each with a short description. The Grant Access button stays off until a profile and email are chosen and while saving.
sections.why: Makes the four levels visible so the owner picks one knowingly.
sections.watch_out: The labels describe what each level does, but the code itself does not enforce those rules. Enforcement depends on the server.

summary: Lets a user see the doctor links they have created and grant or revoke access for caregivers who manage a family member's records.
purpose: Gives the owner one place to manage who can see family health information, both for doctors with temporary links and for caregivers with a registered account.
why: Access to health records needs an easy way to review and cut off. This page is where that control lives for the family area.
how: When the page opens, it loads the doctor share links and the owned family profiles together. The first profile is pre-selected. Revoking a link sends a request and then reloads. Granting caregiver access sends the profile, caregiver email and access level, then closes the form and reloads.
inputs: The user's chosen family profile, a caregiver email typed into a form, an access level choice (VIEW, EDIT, FULL or EMERGENCY), and clicks on Revoke Link, Delegate Caregiver and Grant Access.
outputs: Requests to the server to create caregiver access and to revoke doctor links, plus toast messages and an updated list of links.
risks: The FULL access level is described as full administrative access, which is the broadest choice. Granting it to the wrong email gives that person wide control. The page does not ask the owner to confirm before granting.
debug: If the list does not load, check the requests to the doctor share and family profile endpoints in the browser network tab. If granting fails, the error text comes from the server message or a generic 'User not found' message. If revoke appears to do nothing, the list may not reload, so refresh the page to confirm.
